subject: Reserved capacity QPS anomaly + dedicated pool saturation — exec prioritization requested
content:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: -
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 07:12:00 -0000
Subject: Reserved capacity QPS anomaly + dedicated pool saturation — exec prioritization requested

Team,

Heads-up: Cartflow is reporting a sustained QPS delta from their reserved commitment and we're seeing dedicated GPU pool saturation for their tenant in us-west-2. Frontline ops started an automatic fallback an hour ago, but latency and 5xx rates are rising and the customer is threatening to throttle traffic from their side.

Quick facts:
- Customer: Cartflow (CF-2027-42)
- Observed: 3x reserved QPS (sustained) for the last 40m, token tail-latency up to 1.5s, 5xx at ~2.8% (trend up)
- System: dedicated pool id dp-usw2-17; overflow routing already hit once
- Customer impact: checkout timeouts and repeated retries, revenue-sensitive window in APAC hours for them

Immediate ask: this needs exec-level priority for the next 2 hours — we should (1) approve emergency burst to dedicated-capacity pool, (2) open an ops/eng exec bridge, and (3) send a concise update to Cartflow within 30 minutes.

Attachments: prod_qps_spike.png (current QPS chart), tail_latency.log (latest tails), prod-5xx-sample.txt (sample request IDs)

I'll assemble a short executive note for the bridge. Priyom, can you summarize root signals and mitigation options? Marissa, please align on customer comms / any commercial relief. Jordan — can you authorize burst if needed?

- Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@cartflow.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cartflow Ops <ops@cartflow.com>, Linh Tran <linh.tran@cartflow.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 07:33:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity QPS anomaly + dedicated pool saturation — exec prioritization requested

Naomi — thanks for the quick ping. We're seeing failed checkout flows and an increasing number of merchant rollbacks. Our SRE has collected request ids and logs (attached to this reply). We cannot ramp down traffic from our side without impacting revenue and customers are already swearing us (honestly) — we need a clear timeline for remediation and whether there will be an interruption.

Current symptom summary from Cartflow:
- Traffic burst started ~06:20 PDT; peak sustained beyond committed capacity by ~2.8x
- Errors: 5xx spikes tied to token-service timeouts and OOMs in the inference worker pool
- Priority: reduce tail latency and eliminate 5xx within the hour if possible

Please escalate — we're ready to join a bridge.

— Sam
VP, Engineering — Cartflow

On Tue, 21 Sep 2027 08:05:54 -0000, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: -
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 08:05:54 -0000
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity QPS anomaly + dedicated pool saturation — exec prioritization requested

Quick technical summary from infra:
- Cause signals: a sudden change in client-side prompt mix + long context requests resulted in sustained KV cache growth and increased memory pressure on dp-usw2-17. Several worker pods started to throttle and eviction/restart rates rose.
- Error cause: timed-out inference backend RPCs surfaced as 5xx at the gateway; not a networking issue.
- Short-term mitigations in flight:
  1) Enabled graceful degrade route to a smaller quantized model variant (compatible with Cartflow workload) for low-latency critical paths — deploy started at 08:03Z.
  2) Triggered automatic autoscale-increase for dp-usw2-17 (requesting +2 nodes) — provisioning estimate ~18–22 minutes.
  3) Applied aggressive KV cache TTL reduction for this tenant (drops long-lived prefix entries) — rolling config at 08:07Z.
- Risk/unknown: if prompt sizes stay elevated, autoscale might not catch up; fallback to hosted lower-tier model will impact quality.

Immediate ask for product/exec: approve emergency burst (2x capacity) while autoscale completes and confirm credit/compensation guidance for Marissa to share with customer.

I'll post an ops runbook link and paste key logs to the bridge.

- Priyom
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Naomi / team — I’ve pinged Cartflow leadership and confirmed they will join a bridge at 09:30Z. Customer impact: several merchants have reported abandoned flows; they asked if we can pre-authorize an emergency burst and whether we’d consider a temporary credit for the window if this was on Redwood.

Proposal for external comms (short):
- Acknowledgement: we see the elevated errors and are treating this as top priority.
- Immediate actions: activated lower-latency model variant and autoscale; provisioning for additional nodes underway.
- ETA: preliminary remediation signal expected within 20–30 minutes; full normalization depends on traffic mix and scaling completion.
- Compensation: propose a 20% credit for the impacted hour contingent on final RCA.

Jordan — can you authorize emergency burst while we monitor? If yes I’ll send the customer note and commit to hourly updates.

— Marissa
Account Executive
